html:
Nam Theun 2 is a hydroelectric dam in central Laos that began producing power in 2010. Most of its electricity is sold to Thailand.

Backed by the World Bank after long debate, it was meant to be a model: villagers moved from the flooded plateau got new houses and income plans, and part of the earnings went to health and schools. Critics pointed to lost fisheries and forests.

Laos then built dozens more dams on the Mekong and its tributaries, hoping to become the battery of Southeast Asia. The 2018 collapse of a dam at Xe-Pian Xe-Namnoy, which killed dozens, and the debt from these projects and the railway raised doubts. See also Laotian Civil War.
sum: Nam Theun 2 is a hydroelectric dam in central Laos that began producing power in 2010. Most of its electricity is sold to Thailand.
